chunks: Al-Sakuni narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said:
ʿAli عليه السلام said: “Whoever dies in the crowd of Friday, or Eid, or ʿArafah, or at a well, or on a bridge, and it is not known who killed him, then his blood money is upon the Public Treasury.”

key_terms.بَيْتِ الْمَالِ: the Public Treasury responsible for communal funds
key_terms.زِحَامِ جُمُعَةٍ: the crowd gathered for Friday prayer
key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: the gathering at ʿArafah during hajj
key_terms.عِيدٍ: the Eid gathering or festival prayer occasion

ai.seo_question: Who pays the blood money if a person is killed in a crowd and the killer is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a death occurring in a crowded or public place when the killer cannot be identified. In such a case, the diyah is paid from Bayt al-Mal, reflecting the public authority’s responsibility in unresolved cases involving loss of life.
